Potter County or Randall County?

It depends on which side of the county line the parcel sits, because Amarillo spreads across both. Each county has its own collector and sends its own bill. One appraiser, the Potter-Randall Appraisal District, values property on both sides.

Several taxing units can appear on an Amarillo bill: the City of Amarillo, Amarillo Independent School District, Amarillo Junior College District, the county, and at some addresses Bushland ISD, River Road ISD, Highland Park ISD, Canyon ISD or High Plains Underground Water Conservation District No. 1.

Read a statement as a stack of separate lines. The city line should match the $0.43070 total covered below, and the school, county, college and water district lines each carry their own rates. A parcel in the Canyon ISD or Bushland ISD part of the Amarillo address range shows a different school line from one inside Amarillo ISD.

  • Potter County Tax Assessor-Collector: 900 S. Polk St., Suite 106, Amarillo, 806-342-2600, mail to P.O. Box 2289, Amarillo 79105-2289.
  • Randall County Tax Assessor-Collector: 501 16th St., Suite 200, Canyon, 806-468-5540, mail to P.O. Box 997, Canyon 79015-0997.
  • Potter-Randall Appraisal District: 5701 Hollywood Rd., Amarillo, 806-358-1601, for values, exemptions and protests in both counties.

Market context for sellers

Amarillo had an estimated 205,130 residents in July 2025, up from 200,393 in 2020. Owners occupy about 59.7 percent of homes, and the median home value is $196,900. Renters pay a median of $1,092 a month, and owners with a mortgage pay $1,654, which is the carrying-cost range a buyer will compare against.

City tax rate for 2026/2027

The city's budget news page gives a total of $0.43070 per $100 of valuation. That is $0.32412 for maintenance and operations and $0.10658 for existing debt. Council approved the 2026/2027 budget at that rate by a 4-1 vote at a special meeting in late September 2026.

The budget brings in $2,063,963 more property tax revenue than the year before, a 2.58 percent rise, and $1,295,675 of that increase comes from newly added property. The city describes the maintenance and operations rate as effectively 2.9 percent higher. Randall County's home page carries a similar notice that its rate raises more maintenance and operations tax than the prior year's rate, so Randall-side owners should read both.

The city finance office is at 623 S Johnson St, Suite 2300, phone 806-378-6202, open weekdays 8 to 5. Its Financial Information page lists the rate for each fiscal year.

Due dates and penalties

Notices arrive around October 1. January 31 is the last clean day. From February 1 a penalty starts at 6 percent plus monthly interest, climbing to 12 percent by July.

Older and disabled owners, and disabled former service members, can ask for installments on a homestead bill. If you expect to fall short, call the Potter or Randall office before January 31 and ask what is possible.

Payment goes to whichever county holds your parcel, so check the bill's header to see whether it came from Potter or Randall before you send money. Keep the receipt, because a buyer's agent or a lender may ask for proof that the year is paid.

When you sell, treat January 31 as your own deadline. A paid bill makes the title search cleaner, and the closing agent will not have to hold back money for penalties.

Exemptions through the appraisal district

The district's website runs an online homestead and over-65 portal, a notice-of-estimated-taxes page with a registration option for alerts, and a login portal where owners can see valuations and file appeals or exemptions. A 2026 Disaster Declaration and Exemption item sits at the top of the news feed.

Texas takes $140,000 off a homestead's school value, with another $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners. Local units may add more, so ask what Amarillo, both counties and Amarillo Junior College District have chosen. Disabled former service members qualify on a sliding scale.

  • The ordinary filing cutoff is May 1.
  • Heirs without a deed in their name can claim homestead with an affidavit, a death certificate and a utility bill.

How to protest an appraised value

A protest is written and goes to the appraisal district by May 15, or 30 days after the notice if that is later. Hearings start in mid-May. Only market value can be challenged, and a loss at the board can go to court or arbitration.

One filing covers a parcel on either side of the county line, since the district serves both counties. While the protest is pending, pay the undisputed amount to the Potter or Randall collector before the bill goes delinquent.

The notice you receive shows the value the district set, and the protest form asks what you think is right. Write down a number and the reasons for it. Missing the deadline usually means waiting a year, so file early rather than on the last day.

Prepare before the hearing. Gather recent sales of similar homes, any recent purchase price and photos of defects, and keep copies of what you file.

Tax liens and selling

The lien is created January 1 and stays with the parcel, and the January 1 owner remains personally liable after a sale. Title stays clouded until the taxes are paid. If you own accounts in both counties, for instance on adjoining parcels, ask each tax office for a separate payoff letter before closing.

Before you list, ask the title company to run a tax certificate for the parcel so any open year shows up early. If the house sits on land covered by more than one account, make sure each account is listed in the payoff request. That avoids a surprise at the closing table.

The title company usually orders the payoff figure and pays it from the sale money. A cash buyer skips the lender's checks, but the tax payoff still has to be cleared before the deed is recorded.

Tax sales

Taxing units can foreclose and sell through the constable or an agent. There is no statewide sale calendar, so watch the Potter and Randall county sites and clerk postings. A homestead owner keeps a redemption right for two years after the buyer's deed is filed, at a premium that rises in the second year. Other property has a shorter window. If you are behind and need to sell, closing before a foreclosure sale lets you keep the equity.

Frequently asked questions

Is Amarillo in Potter County or Randall County?

Both. The city spans the line, and the bill comes from whichever county holds the parcel. The Potter-Randall Appraisal District values property in both.

What is the Amarillo city tax rate for 2026?

The total is $0.43070 per $100 of valuation. That is $0.32412 for maintenance and operations and $0.10658 for debt.

When do Amarillo property taxes go delinquent?

February 1, after a January 31 due date. A 6 percent penalty plus interest starts that day and climbs to 12 percent by July 1.

Who do I call to pay my taxes?

Call the county office for your parcel: Potter County at 806-342-2600 or Randall County at 806-468-5540. For value and exemption questions, call the appraisal district at 806-358-1601.

How big is the homestead exemption?

$140,000 comes off the school tax value, plus $60,000 for seniors or disabled owners. Local units may add more.

Who values and who bills

Two county offices handle a Brownsville home, and they are easy to confuse. Cameron Appraisal District staff appraise the property from an office in San Benito. The Cameron County Tax Assessor-Collector mails a single combined bill covering the county, the school district, the cities and special districts. The appraisal district holds no tax amounts and takes no payments.

The district's website offers a property search, a map search and a Truth in Taxation portal. Texas levies no state property tax, so every rate on a Brownsville bill traces to a local body.

Tax rates for 2026

The county's Truth in Taxation summary prints a rate per $100 of taxable value for each unit that touches most Brownsville homes. The table sets 2026 beside 2025.

The city line splits into $0.353581 for maintenance and operations and $0.249923 for debt. Its no-new-revenue rate reads $0.563407 and its voter-approval rate $0.613440. The school district's line has fallen a long way from the $1.208690 it printed for 2022.

Drainage districts, municipal utility districts and other special districts add their own levy, so read every line on your bill. The city has also posted a notice of intent to issue certificates of obligation up to $27,000,000, to be paid from property tax and landfill surplus revenue, and it lists $355,576,000 in outstanding debt principal. Those debt figures explain part of the debt portion of the city rate.

What a late bill costs

Payment is due January 31 on bills mailed around October 1. Starting February 1, a six percent penalty plus one percent interest apply, which the county office sums up as seven percent.

  • Each month adds a point of penalty, topping out at 12 percent in July.
  • A taxing unit that brings in a collection lawyer can tack on as much as 20 percent.
  • Tax Code 33.011 lets an owner request a waiver, generally if payment comes within 21 days of learning the bill was late.

An owner who is elderly, disabled, or a disabled former service member or surviving spouse, and who claims a homestead, can pay in four parts: January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. The office posts its card and e-check fees, which are 3 percent for cards, $1.00 for an e-check of $5,000 or less and $3.00 above that.

Homestead exemptions

School taxes drop on the first $140,000 of a homestead's value, with $60,000 more off the school bill for an owner who is elderly or disabled. Appraised value of a homestead can climb only 10 percent a year.

A school tax ceiling for a senior can follow the owner to another Texas homestead, though it rises after additions such as a pool, garage or room. An owner picks either over-65 or disabled status, not both, and each spouse files with proof of Texas residency.

One local layer is new. The Brownsville Navigation District, the Port of Brownsville, approved a full homestead exemption for qualifying owners who are elderly or disabled. The city's September 2026 notice says it starts with the 2027 tax year and covers Brownsville, Rancho Viejo, Los Fresnos, Indian Lake and Starbase. Disabled former service members may qualify for a partial exemption, and a 100 percent rating brings a full one. Forms go to the appraisal district by April 30, and Form 50-114 covers the homestead types.

How to protest your appraisal

A protest must be written. Mail it, deliver it, fax it to (956) 399-6969 or email protest@cameroncad.org. The mailing address is PO Box 1010, San Benito, TX 78586, and the postmark has to land inside the window: the later of May 15 and the thirtieth day after the value notice. No official form is needed, only the owner, the property and a statement that you disagree.

  • Informal hearings with an appraiser: walk-ins run from April 14 to May 16, first come first served, and requested ones happen by phone.
  • Formal hearing: usually three members, about 15 minutes, with at least 15 days of notice.
  • One postponement is allowed without a showing of cause if you named no agent.
  • An appeal can go to district court, binding arbitration under limited conditions, or in Cameron County to the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

The board rules on January 1 market value only. Service quality and tax rates are outside its reach. Without a timely protest neither the appraiser nor the board can change the value. Every property is reappraised at least every third year, and a notice is not required when the increase is $1,000 or less.

Market context for sellers

Brownsville had an estimated 192,957 residents in 2025, a 3.6 percent rise since the 2020 count. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $139,900, and owners occupy 61.7 percent of homes. Typical rent is $923. The Brownsville Navigation District and Texas Southmost College both levy their own tax, so expect a separate line for each on your bill.

Records, liens and selling

A sale can fund with taxes owing, because the title company gets a payoff from the tax office and pays it. The January 1 owner remains personally liable for that year's bill even after a later sale.

Copies of deeds, plats and mortgage records come from the Cameron County Clerk at 835 E. Levee St., Brownsville, (956) 544-0815, not from the appraisal district. A change of ownership needs a recorded instrument or volume and page. Mobile homes need a Statement of Ownership and Location before the land and home combine on one bill. Land taken out of agricultural use triggers a rollback tax owed by whoever holds title then.

If a bill is already late, ask the Cameron tax office about a payment agreement. Some collectors allow up to 36 months, and a plan is required for a residence homestead. After a collection suit starts, court costs join the bill. Foreclosure sales are public auctions with no statewide list, so look for notices from the county clerk and tax office.

Keep your paid receipts for recent years in one folder. A buyer's agent or the title company may ask for them, and having them ready makes it easier to prove that nothing is owed and that exemptions are on the account.

Before you list, ask the tax office for the balance on every account tied to the parcel and the title company for a payoff. A cash buyer skips lender review, yet still needs the tax account clear at closing.

Frequently asked questions

Which taxing unit has the highest 2026 rate?

Brownsville ISD, at $0.771600 per $100 of taxable value, ahead of the city at $0.603504 and the county at $0.424393 in the county's summary table.

On what date is a Brownsville tax bill late?

February 1, for anything unpaid after January 31. Penalty and interest begin then, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

Can I email an appraisal protest?

Yes. The appraisal district accepts written protests by email at protest@cameroncad.org, by fax, by mail or by hand. Mailed protests must carry a postmark by the deadline.

Do older homeowners get anything from the port district?

Yes. The Brownsville Navigation District approved a full homestead exemption for owners who are elderly or disabled, beginning with the 2027 tax year. Apply through the appraisal district.

Which office holds my deed?

The Cameron County Clerk, 835 E. Levee St., Brownsville, (956) 544-0815. The appraisal district keeps no deeds.

City of Killeen tax rate

Treat this as one line of several. Bell County, the school system and any special district covering your street each add their own rate, and your final bill turns on your taxable value and exemptions. The rate sets the price per $100 of value; the city's budget is a different document that shows how the money is spent.

Who values your house and takes payment

Killeen has a single office for both value and payment, the Tax Appraisal District of Bell County. Start at bellcad.org, where the city's tax page points you. The site has the property search, exemption forms, payment choices and truth-in-taxation material. A Bell County parcel number is the key to any bill question.

Your payment choices:

  • Card or check by phone or web, with a vendor fee; an electronic check runs $0.50.
  • Check, cash or money order at any district counter, free of charge.
  • The outside drop box at the Belton office, for after-hours payments.

Paying early earns a discount of 3 percent through October 31, 2 percent through November 30 and 1 percent through December 31. A weekend deadline slides to Monday. Look up the schedule on the district's site each fall before you plan around it.

The district's site also carries a Truth in Taxation page with the latest rate information, a short explainer titled "What's in my property tax bill," and a PDF on tax deferral. Read the deferral explainer before you assume it fits your account. The property search lets you view tax statements and amounts due.

When Killeen property tax becomes late

Missing the January 31 cutoff makes a bill delinquent the next day. A 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest are added then, and both grow month by month into July. When a collector hires a private attorney, up to 20 percent more can follow. Since fall payments earn a discount, an early check usually beats a January one.

A payoff statement matters in a sale because each January 1 puts a lien on the house. Get the number from the district ahead of closing, and find out whether this year's bill has gone out.

Help exists for owners who have slipped. You can ask in writing, inside 181 days of the delinquency date, for the penalty to be waived. Seniors, disabled owners and disabled veteran owners with a homestead may split the bill into four payments. Some collectors also write plans running up to 36 months.

Exemptions that cut a Killeen bill

Filing for a homestead exemption costs nothing, and most Killeen owners use it. The district recognizes these categories:

  • Your home as a residence homestead
  • A disabled person
  • Anyone 65 or older, or that person's surviving spouse
  • A 100 percent disabled veteran or surviving spouse
  • The surviving spouse of a service member killed in action
  • The surviving spouse of a first responder who died on duty
  • A residence donated to a partially disabled veteran or surviving spouse

The application needs a current driver's license or Texas ID. Disabled persons add a Social Security Administration letter or A&B card, and disabled veteran applicants add a recent VA awards letter. You do not renew each year, although the chief appraiser can request a fresh application. Past April 30? File anyway, because once approved the district gives whatever late-filing relief the law permits.

State school exemptions stack on top. A homestead gets $140,000, and seniors and disabled owners get $60,000 beyond that. Disabled veteran exemptions run between $5,000 and $12,000 depending on rating, and a 100 percent rating can erase the homestead's taxable value.

The Killeen homestead cap

Tax Code 23.23 caps yearly growth in a homestead's appraised value at 10 percent, starting the January 1 after the exemption first applies. Those capped steps continue until assessed value catches market value, which is why a home owned a long time can be taxed on much less than it would sell for.

A buyer does not inherit the seller's cap, because the new owner's value is measured fresh after the sale. Notices for homesteads go out around April 1, and protests are generally due in mid-May.

Seniors and disabled owners also get school tax frozen at the first qualifying year's amount, with the ceiling adjusting in proportion if they move to another Texas homestead. A city or county can adopt a matching limit, so find out what your account carries.

Killeen housing in brief

The city counts 161,883 residents, 5.7 percent more than in 2020. Just under half of homes, 49.5 percent, are owner-occupied, so rentals make up the rest. The middle owned home is valued at $215,400, middle gross rent is $1,208 and middle household income is $60,977. The city has a large military population, which makes the disabled veteran exemptions above worth checking.

Selling a Killeen house when tax is owed

Call the district first and ask for a payoff that includes earlier years, plus a date for this year's bill. Check that the homestead exemption is on record; an unfiled one costs less to correct before you list. Give the figures to the title company, which settles the balance out of your sale proceeds and shares the current year with the buyer.

The order of work is short. Get the payoff, confirm exemptions, resolve any penalty request, and pass the figures to the title company. Each step takes a phone call or a form, so starting a few weeks ahead of an offer keeps the closing date safe. Ask the district whether it can email the statement, so you have a written figure to show the buyer.

Behind on the bill? Raise the waiver request and installment options before you list. Taking a cash offer as-is spares you repairs and showings, yet the tax lien is still settled at the table. Bring your latest statement, your exemption confirmation and your parcel number to the first title company call, so the payoff and the closing statement agree.

Frequently asked questions

What did Killeen adopt as its city rate?

The adopted fiscal year 2027 rate is 73.01 cents per $100 of taxable value, made up of 55.62 cents for maintenance and operations and 17.39 cents for debt service. County, school and special district rates are added on the same bill.

Who do I pay Killeen property tax to?

Pay through the Tax Appraisal District of Bell County, which offers online, phone and in-person options and a drop box at its Belton office. Match the parcel and account number on your bill to the district's property search before you send money.

When is Killeen property tax delinquent?

February 1 is the first delinquent day for tax unpaid after January 31. A penalty and interest start that day and keep growing into July.

Does Bell County give a discount for early payment?

Yes. The district lists a 3 percent discount through October 31, 2 percent through November 30 and 1 percent through December 31, and a weekend deadline moves to Monday.

Where is a Killeen homestead exemption filed?

File the free application with the Tax Appraisal District of Bell County. Bring a current driver's license or Texas ID, and add disability or VA paperwork if it applies. No yearly renewal is required.

Mesquite sits partly in Dallas County and partly in Kaufman County. Before dialing anyone, identify which county your parcel belongs to, because that county decides who values the house and who collects. A separate rate table for each side appears on the city's tax page.

The state itself collects no property tax. Each January 1 a county appraisal district assigns the house a value. Five local bodies, ranging from the city to Parkland Hospital, then tax that value at their own rates.

After January 31

Bills go in the mail during October, and you can pay as soon as one arrives. In Dallas County an account is late after January 31, and a mailed check is judged by its postmark. A statement that never reached you is no excuse for the tax or the late charges.

February 1 is when the damage starts: a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest land on the account. After that, interest gains a point each month with no ceiling, and the penalty gains a point each month until it stops at 12 percent in July.

Exemptions that shrink the bill

Age is the first lever. Homeowners over 65 get a $65,000 city exemption, disabled persons get $15,000, and a person qualifies for only one. Either also locks in a ceiling: city and school taxes stay at the first qualifying year's amount until you add to the house or move.

School taxes get a separate state break: $140,000 off a residence homestead, and $60,000 beyond that for older or disabled owners.

  • A disabled veteran exemption starts at $5,000 for a 10 to 29 percent rating and reaches $12,000 at 70 to 100 percent. At a 100 percent rating, the homestead can be exempt entirely.
  • A homestead's appraised value can grow only 10 percent a year, with the limit starting the year after the first exemption.
  • An heir who is not on the recorded deed must give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

When to file a value protest

Send the written protest to the Appraisal Review Board. May 15 is the cutoff, unless your notice arrived late, in which case you have 30 days from delivery. Homestead owners hear around April 1; owners of other property hear around May 1.

Dallas County's tax office refers all protest questions to the appraisal districts. A Dallas County parcel is disputed at Dallas Central Appraisal District and a Kaufman County parcel at Kaufman Central Appraisal District. A loss at the board still leaves options: district court, binding arbitration, or, for values above $1,000,000, the State Office of Administrative Hearings. Whatever you pick, pay the undisputed part of the tax by the cutoff, or penalties will not be held back.

Mesquite housing at a glance

The city's population is 150,693, about the same as the 150,108 counted in 2020. Of all homes, 62.8 percent are owner-occupied, with a middle value of $245,700. Middle rent is $1,513 and middle household income is $72,537. Residents 65 and older, who qualify for the city's bigger exemption, make up 11.3 percent.

Working out your own number

A quick way to size up a Mesquite bill is to find your parcel on the right appraisal district site, note the taxable value after exemptions, and multiply by the rate for each unit on the table above, one line at a time. Your parcel's own total is the figure that counts, and the district's printout is easier to trust than a rule of thumb. If something looks wrong, such as a missing homestead exemption or an old owner name, call the district now rather than in the spring.

Owners with a mortgage should also ask the lender whether it pays from escrow, and for which taxing units. Where the lender pays only part of the bill, the owner is responsible for the rest. A missed unit is a common reason a delinquent notice turns up on an account that looked paid.

What a Mesquite seller should check before closing

Whoever is on title January 1 carries that year's lien, so a March closing still leaves the seller answerable for the full year. Ask the title company how it will split the bill with the buyer, and study the payoff lines in its commitment.

A buyer who closes after January 1 and whose seller never had a homestead exemption can apply right away. For your balance, call the Dallas County Tax Office, or the Kaufman County office if the parcel is on that side.

If the collection attorney already has the account, request a written payoff that itemizes penalty, interest and court costs. The title company uses that number to clear the lien at funding.

Pull together each taxing unit's newest statement, proof of your homestead exemption if you have one, and any protest papers from spring. An open protest matters: a win changes the tax figure on the closing statement, so tell the title company and give the buyer the hearing date. Hold on to receipts for earlier years too, since a title company may want proof they were paid.

Why does the Kaufman County side of Mesquite show a higher total rate?

Only the county line changes. The city's table shows 0.2155000 for Dallas County and 0.4275260 for Kaufman County, which produces totals of 2.3456670 and 2.5576930.

Until what date can Mesquite taxes be paid without charges?

January 31. Charges begin February 1 and grow each month into July.

How much does Mesquite exempt for homeowners over 65?

The city exempts $65,000 for owners over 65 and $15,000 for disabled persons, and one person gets only one of the two. Mesquite ISD applies its own state-mandated amounts.

Where do I pick up a homestead exemption form for a house in Mesquite?

Call the appraisal district for your county, Dallas Central at 214-631-0520 or Kaufman Central at 972-932-6081. The city's tax office does not issue them.

Can a Mesquite house with unpaid taxes still be sold?

Yes. The title company gets a payoff from the collection attorney and pays it at closing, since the lien follows the property until then.

Offices that handle McAllen property tax

McAllen is in Hidalgo County, and a McAllen bill usually stacks the city, the county, a school district such as McAllen ISD and South Texas College, with special districts on some parcels. The Hidalgo County Appraisal District sets values. The City of McAllen Tax Office sends the city's own statement.   • Hidalgo County: $0.57500

  • South Texas College: $0.16200

The city's own 2025 rate is $0.448989 per $100, as printed on its tax notice. Add them together for a full-rate picture, then subtract any exemptions on your file. Mail for the city tax office goes to P.O. Box 220, McAllen, TX 78505-0220.

Payment deadline and late charges

Texas gives McAllen owners until January 31 to pay. A deadline that falls on a weekend slides to the next business day, and statements usually go out in October. For the 2026 bill, the last penalty-free day is Monday, February 1, 2027.

Charges begin on February 1. Interest adds one percentage point each month until the account is paid, and the schedule continues past July, reaching a 24 percent total the following January.

The city's slice is one piece of the total. The county, school district and college each set their own rates every fall, and taxing units have until about September 29, or 60 days after they receive the certified roll if that is later, to do so.

Exemptions that reduce a McAllen bill

The city offers $10,000 for each owner who has reached 65, $10,000 for a disabled person, and $5,000 to $12,000 for a disabled veteran depending on rating. A 100 percent disabled veteran's residence homestead is fully exempt. Applications and address corrections go to the chief appraiser at the Hidalgo County Appraisal District.

  • Older or disabled owners: $60,000 more comes off school taxes, and the school tax bill on that home generally cannot climb after the owner qualifies.
  • Value cap: a homestead's appraised value may rise at most 10 percent per year, starting the January after the exemption begins.
  • Filing window: most exemption applications are due before May 1, though disabled veteran applicants may file later.

Someone who buys after January 1 can sometimes claim the exemption right away if the seller never received it.

Installments and ways to pay

Homeowners who are 65 or over, disabled, or disabled veteran owners with a homestead exemption can split the bill into four equal parts with no penalty or interest by asking no later than January 31.   • Drop box: the tax office has payment flaps, one inside the lobby and one outside on the Cedar Avenue side. Put the payment and a copy of your statement in a sealed envelope, and leave cash out.
  • Email bills: owners who enroll in eNotification before October 17 get that year's bill by email.

When a mortgage company pays from escrow, the lender must tell the tax office which accounts it covers, and unpaid accounts get a courtesy reminder in mid-January. Never receiving the bill does not waive the penalty.

A protest must reach the Hidalgo County appraisal review board by May 15 or, if your notice arrives late, within 30 days of delivery. Homestead notices are mailed about April 1 and other property notices about May 1. Hearings begin around mid-May.

After the board rules, you can sue in district court, ask for binding arbitration or, for values above $1,000,000, take the case to SOAH, the State Office of Administrative Hearings. An appeal generally stays valid only if the undisputed portion of the tax is paid before it turns delinquent.

Selling a McAllen house when you owe tax

Back taxes are normally cleared at closing, because delinquent tax stands in the way of clean title. A lien for each year's tax attaches on January 1, and whoever owns the house that day remains liable for that year's tax after a sale.

Texas offers relief before things reach that point. Penalty and interest can sometimes be waived: the request goes in writing before day 181 after delinquency, and the tax itself must be paid within 21 days of the owner learning of the debt. Some collectors allow plans stretching to 36 months, and a residence homestead must be offered one. For questions about delinquent notices, the collection law firm at Lone Star Plaza, 1512 S Lone Star Wy, Edinburg, (956) 383-4500, has a Hidalgo County office.

Behind on the bill and thinking of a fast as-is sale? Send the property address and the balance on your statement. Ask the tax office for an itemized payoff first, so you know what the title company will pay from your proceeds.

The City of McAllen's 2025 rate is $0.448989 per $100 of value, and the 2026 proposal repeats it. Hidalgo County, McAllen ISD and South Texas College add their own rates, which the county tax office publishes on its rate schedule.

January 31 is the annual deadline, and a weekend date slides to the next business day. Penalties begin the day after the deadline.

Does McAllen offer a homeowner exemption?

The city offers $10,000 for owners 65 or older and $10,000 for disabled persons, plus disabled veteran exemptions, but no percentage homestead exemption. McAllen ISD applies the statewide $140,000 residence homestead exemption.

Can I pay McAllen property taxes in installments?

Yes, for homeowners past 65, disabled homeowners and disabled veteran owners who hold a residence homestead exemption and ask by January 31. Four equal payments fall due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31.

Value questions go to the Hidalgo County Appraisal District at (956) 381-8466. The City of McAllen Tax Office handles billing at (956) 681-1330.

Card payments carry a 2.19% fee and electronic checks a $1.50 flat fee, both going to the payment vendor. Credit card payments need only the account number. An electronic check needs the account number and bank details. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and American Express are accepted.

Who values and bills a house in Midland

In Midland County a single agency handles valuation and billing. That agency, the Midland Central Appraisal District, appraises every parcel and mails the statements. It works from 4631 Andrews Hwy and answers at 432-699-4991 on weekdays between 8 and 5.

Roughly 548,842 statements for the 2026 tax year went into the mail on October 23, 2026. If your parcel is across the line in Martin County, a different office appraises and bills it. Call the Martin County tax office in that case.

Think of four roles. The district sets the value. A review board hears disputes. Each taxing unit (city, school, county, college, hospital) picks its own budget and rate. A collector then multiplies and sends out the bill.

2025 and 2026 tax rates

The City of Midland moved from $0.347999 per $100 in 2025 to $0.383092 in 2026, and the county, the college and the hospital all went up too. Midland ISD stayed flat at 0.841500.

A statement can be paid the day it arrives. Collection opens around October 1, and nothing extra is added until February 1. That morning the unpaid balance is hit with six percent in penalty and one percent in interest. The penalty grows by a point every month and levels off at twelve percent once July arrives. Homestead and other exemptions

Midland ISD takes $140,000 off a homestead. The City of Midland has no general homestead amount, but it does help older owners with $8,000 for age 65 or older.

  • The county's optional homestead percentage is set at 3 percent with a $5,000 floor, though $0 is actually granted.
  • A disabled veteran receives $5,000, $7,500, $10,000 or $12,000 by disability bracket, and a 100 percent rating covers the full homesteadable value.

Exemptions belong to the person who owned on January 1, which means a buyer closing later in the year has to file fresh. How to challenge a Midland value

The notice describes the property, shows its value and exemptions, and estimates the tax. Values shift when comparable sales move or when a record is corrected for a measurement or a pool, so read the description line by line before you protest.

Still unhappy after the board rules? Court, binding arbitration and (for values over $1,000,000) the State Office of Administrative Hearings are open to you. Unpaid tax does not stop a sale. Closing staff request a payoff figure that includes tax, penalty, interest and any lawyer's fee. That number is deducted from your sale check. You do not have to pay anything up front unless you prefer to.

Midland has grown fast. The city counted 132,524 residents in 2020 and now estimates 147,615 for July 2025, a gain of 11.1 percent. About 65.1 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, and a typical one is valued at $319,200. Those figures cover the whole city, and individual streets can run well above or below them, so the appraisal record for your own parcel matters more than any average.

What a Midland seller should do about property tax

Look up your account at the appraisal district before you list, since that one office both values the house and sends the bill. Each January 1 a lien attaches, and whoever owned the house that morning is responsible for the year's tax no matter when the deed moves.

  • Find out from the title company how the current year's tax will be divided between you and the buyer.
  • Your buyer should file a new homestead application, because the exemption now on file is yours.
  • On a delinquent account, request a payoff that shows penalty, interest and any attorney fee.
  • Inherited house? An heir whose name is on no recorded deed can still claim the exemption by giving the district an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

Because the city rate rose between 2025 and 2026 while the school rate held steady, a buyer comparing your 2026 statement with an older one will see a bigger city share. Keep both years' statements handy and point the buyer to the district's rate page. A cash sale removes the lender's appraisal and repair demands, but the tax payoff still gets settled at closing.

The City of Midland's 2026 rate is $0.383092 per $100 of taxable value, up from $0.347999 in 2025. The school, county, college and hospital rates are added to it.

Who sends Midland County tax statements?

The Midland Central Appraisal District mails them. You can reach it at 4631 Andrews Hwy or 432-699-4991. For a Martin County parcel, call the Martin County tax office.

Does the City of Midland grant a regular homestead exemption?

No general amount, only $8,000 for owners 65 or older at the city level. Midland ISD exempts $140,000 of a homestead.

Is it too late to claim a homestead exemption I forgot?

Maybe not. Late applications are taken for a year after the bill goes delinquent, but nobody files it for you.

From February 1 the balance carries six percent penalty and one percent interest. Penalty hits twelve percent in July, interest keeps accruing, and a lawyer's fee of up to 20 percent may follow.

Who values, who taxes

Taylor Central Appraisal District puts a value on each parcel in Abilene and the rest of the county. Rates come from elsewhere: the city, the county, the school district and any other unit levy their own. The appraisal office decides market value and nothing else, so it cannot change a rate or the total you owe.

Visit 1534 S Treadaway Blvd, Abilene on a weekday, write to P.O. Box 1800, or call (325) 676-9381. Forms can be left in the drop box out front. Send exemption forms to exemptions@cadtx.org and protest forms to arbprotest@cadtx.org.

The district hears about a new owner once the deed is recorded with the county clerk. Giving the district the recorded document number, or emailing a scan to customerservice@cadtx.org, speeds up the ownership change.

City tax rate, fiscal 2027

Abilene's council set the city rate at 74.95 cents per $100 of taxable value, a hair under the prior 75.06 cents, when it approved the $414.6 million operating budget on Sept. 10, 2026. The fiscal year starts Oct. 1.

A rate cut does not shrink every bill. The city estimates an average 4.2 percent tax increase on existing property because values rose, and new construction accounts for $16.8 million of the $18.3 million increase in total property tax revenue. The city's home page adds that the adopted rate brings in more maintenance and operations revenue than last year's rate did.

Your statement also has county, school and other lines, which means the city figure is just one slice.

Due dates and penalties

Statements go out in October and are payable when received, yet most owners can hold off until Jan. 31 and owe nothing extra. Any balance left on Feb. 1 is delinquent, and that day it picks up a six percent penalty plus one percent interest.

Each month adds another point of penalty until it tops out at 12 percent on July 1, while interest continues at a point monthly. Taxing units that hire a collection attorney may add as much as 20 percent. Homeowners who are older or disabled may pay a homestead bill in four installments, and some collectors allow payment plans of up to 36 months on a delinquent residence homestead.

Selling soon? Pay before Feb. 1 if you can. Penalties and interest land on whoever holds title as they build, and the title company will want a clean account.

Homestead exemption and others

If you own the house and live in it on Jan. 1, the general homestead exemption is yours for the asking, free of charge. No one needs to be hired to file it, and it stays in place from year to year unless the district writes to request a fresh application or you move.

  • Turning 65: the extra exemption is added on its own when the district already has your birth date, and applying at any point in that year earns the full year.
  • Mobile home on land you do not own: include the title or a verified purchase contract.
  • Home with a business inside: a homestead apportionment may be available.
  • Nonprofits: federal tax-exempt status does not bring an automatic exemption, and applications are due by April 30.

State law lets school districts deduct $140,000 from a homestead's value, plus a further $60,000 when the owner is older or disabled. Disabled former service members follow a separate sliding scale, with a full exemption at a 100 percent rating.

How to protest your appraisal

Only market value can be protested. Assessed value is formula-driven, and a big bill caused by a big rate gives you nothing to argue. Notices of appraised value arrive around April 1. The usual cutoff is May 31, or a month after your notice if that comes later, and the date is printed on the notice itself.

Submit by mail, email, drop box or the online portal. An informal meeting with an appraiser may come first, and if you accept a value there the case is over. If not, the formal hearing is held at the Treadaway Boulevard office, and you are told at least 15 days beforehand.

  • Bring paper copies of comparable sales, a recent purchase price and photos of defects.
  • Expect three to five minutes per side and about 15 minutes in the room.
  • One postponement is allowed if no agent represents you.
  • Skipping the hearing gets the protest dismissed, and you have four days to ask for a reopening.

Landlords and small business owners also deal with the district's business personal property side. Renditions listing furniture, equipment and inventory are due by April 15. An extension to May 15 needs a written request by April 15, and skipping the filing brings a 10 percent penalty on the taxes ultimately imposed. Rendition forms are on the district's Forms page.

Before you file, read your notice carefully, compare it with what similar houses near you sold for, and decide what value you can support with paper evidence. A protest that comes with comparable sales and photos is far easier for a board to act on than one that only says the number feels high. Keep copies of everything you submit, and note the date you filed.

If you lose at the board, the next options are district court, binding arbitration or, for values above $1 million, the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

Selling with taxes owed

A tax lien for the year attaches January 1, which means a later sale still carries that year's bill. Title companies typically pay it from the seller's money. Buyers should check which exemptions sit on the account before closing.

New owners can claim their own homestead for the rest of the tax year if the previous owner did not. The 10 percent yearly limit on assessed value begins the year after an exemption is first granted, so the new owner's clock starts fresh.

A seller can work in this order. Ask the title company early which year is unpaid. Pay anything delinquent so penalties stop, or approve payment from your proceeds. After closing, pass the recorded deed number to the appraisal district so the new owner's name shows on the account. Cash buyers can close fast, though the title company still clears the lien at the table. Keep your paid receipts and your exemption confirmation with the closing file, since a buyer may ask for them.

Frequently asked questions

Who sets the property tax rate in Abilene?

Each taxing unit does. Abilene's council set the city rate of 74.95 cents per $100 for fiscal 2027, and the county, school district and other units set theirs. Taylor CAD only values property.

Can I protest my Abilene tax bill?

Not the bill itself. You can protest market value with Taylor CAD, normally by May 31 or a month after your notice. The rate is outside its control.

Where is the Taylor Central Appraisal District?

The school line varies too. Pearland ISD, Alvin ISD and Friendswood ISD all serve parts of the county, so the school charge on your own bill shows which district covers your street.

Pearland tax calendar

Every Texas taxing unit follows one statewide calendar anchored on New Year's Day. On that date both the property's value and its owner are fixed for the year.

  • January 1: value is set, and that year's lien takes hold.
  • April 1 or soon after: notices of appraised value start going to single-family homesteads, with other property following near May 1.

An account still open on the first of February is charged six percent penalty and one percent interest. After that the penalty grows monthly and reaches twelve percent on July 1, with interest still ticking up. Where a unit has hired a collection lawyer, a fee of as much as 20 percent can follow.

Protest hearings before the appraisal review board begin around May 15. The board is expected to approve the records by July 20 unless more than five percent of total value is still under protest. Homesteads are protected from fast value jumps too. From the January after the first exemption, appraised value may rise no more than 10 percent annually. Seniors and disabled owners can also cap their school tax, and the cap follows them to a new Texas homestead.

A disabled veteran may exempt part of one property. The scale by VA disability rating runs like this:

  • Rating of 30 to 49 percent: as high as $7,500
  • Rating of 50 to 69 percent: as high as $10,000

Selling a Pearland house with unpaid taxes

Back tax follows the lot, not the seller. A fresh lien starts every January 1 and delinquent amounts block clear title for a buyer. Even after a sale, the person who owned the house on that date can be sued over that year's bill.

Late charges can often be waived. Pay the tax by the 21st day after you learn it was delinquent and get a written request in before day 181. A residence homestead owner can ask for a payment plan, and some collectors allow 36 months. While an appraisal appeal is pending, keep the undisputed amount current before the delinquency date.

If a lawsuit ends in a sale, a former homestead owner can buy back within two years of the purchaser's deed filing, and other land within 180 days. Surplus proceeds stay claimable by the former owner for two years.

Gather these before you list: your latest bill from the county that holds the parcel, any exemption confirmation, and a note of which school district serves the address. A buyer's agent will ask about utility district charges, so find out whether your neighborhood has one.

The sequence is short. Get a written payoff from the county holding your parcel, pass it to the title company, and let closing clear the older years first. Then work out with the buyer how this year is divided.

Both. The city is a taxing unit in each appraisal district, and where your parcel sits determines which one appraises it.

Anything unpaid after January 31 becomes delinquent on February 1, when penalty and interest begin. By July 1 the penalty stands at twelve percent.

Richardson does not offer the optional percentage homestead exemption, so nothing shows for it on the city's line of a Collin or Dallas County statement. Only school districts must grant a homestead exemption. Other units choose whether to adopt one.

The city does give a senior exemption of $160,000. Do not apply at city hall. The form goes to the appraisal district for the county where the property lies. State rules add more:

  • Richardson ISD, like every school district, must give the $140,000 residence homestead exemption.

  • Once a homestead qualifies, yearly growth in its appraised value is limited to ten percent.

  • A homeowner with a 100 percent VA rating is fully exempt on the residence homestead.

Late payment penalties

Nothing extra is due through January 31. From February 1 an unpaid balance carries a six percent penalty and a one percent interest charge. Each month brings one more point of penalty, topping out at twelve percent in July, and interest has no top. Attorney fees as high as 20 percent are possible when a unit has a collection lawyer.

Paying in two halves is allowed, the first at the end of November and the second at the end of June. Older or disabled homestead owners get four installments, and a late installment draws a six percent penalty. Forgiveness of penalty and interest can be requested if you pay within 21 days of learning the account was delinquent and the written request is in before day 181.

Protesting your appraisal

An appraisal protest runs on a separate clock. File by May 15, or by the 30th day after the notice is delivered if that is later. Until the dispute ends, send at least the undisputed tax before February 1 so no penalty builds. Gather recent sales of similar Richardson houses before the hearing, and note anything in the property description that is wrong. Bring the notice itself, since it shows the value and exemptions the board will start from.

Back tax and a Richardson sale

A tax lien forms each January 1 and stays on the property through any sale. The title company will insist on past-due amounts being paid at closing, because a buyer cannot get clear title until they are. Whoever owned on that January 1 is also still liable for the year's bill.

Utility accounts matter at the same time. Richardson's utility customer service line is 972-744-4120. The 2026-27 budget changed how residential wastewater is calculated, using only the prior year's November through February water use and leaving out the highest month. A seller who is closing should call customer service about ending the account so the final bill is settled. Customers over 65 with a 3/4-inch or 1-inch meter keep the old $8 base charge.

Street work can touch a listing too. The city has reported sanitary sewer rehabilitation near the Promenade Shopping Center off Coit Road and in the Berkner Park neighborhood. Crews use pipe bursting and pipe lining, which keeps road closures minor and needs fewer construction vehicles. If your house is nearby, mention it to buyers before they find out on their own.

If a taxing unit sues and sells the house, a former homestead owner has two years from the filing of the buyer's deed to buy it back, and other property 180 days. An heir selling an inherited Richardson house should record the right paperwork first: a muniment of title order, an executor's deed, or an affidavit of death paired with a transfer on death deed.

Selling with taxes owed

Past-due tax rarely kills a deal. Request a written payoff from the county tax office for your parcel and hand it to the title company, which pays the old years from your sale money. For the current year, the settlement sheet needs to say who pays what, because the January 1 owner is on the hook for it.

Before a sale date arrives, collect the most recent statement from each taxing unit, proof of any exemption and your utility account details, so nothing delays the closing. A seller who needs speed may prefer a cash buyer, who does away with the lender's timeline. The tax balance still gets cleared at the table.

Richardson housing at a glance

Richardson counted 99,223 people in 2010 and 119,469 in 2020. The 2025 estimate of 118,542 is a 0.8 percent dip from 2020. Owners occupy 50.7 percent of homes, so the city splits almost evenly between owners and renters. A typical owned home is worth $431,400, rent runs $1,857 at the median and median household income is $98,111.

It depends on the county that holds your parcel, since Richardson lies partly in Dallas County and partly in Collin County. Each office has its own address and phone.

What is Richardson's property tax rate?

The city's 2026-27 rate is $0.54218 per $100 of assessed valuation, the same as the year before. Richardson ISD, the county and other units add their own rates.

Does Richardson have a senior exemption?

Yes. The $160,000 senior property tax exemption continues in 2026-27. Ask the appraisal district for your county how to apply.

When does Richardson property tax become delinquent?

The February 1 after the tax year ends. The 2026 tax, for instance, is mailed in October 2026 and goes delinquent February 1, 2027.

Can I sell a Richardson house that has back taxes?

Yes. Closing normally pays the old tax from your proceeds, which gives the buyer clear title. List on the settlement sheet who covers each part of the current year.

Values come from a different body, the Jefferson Central Appraisal District, and the bills are built on them.

One bill can carry many layers. Past the county, city and school district, the list may include the Port of Beaumont Authority, the Sabine-Neches Navigation District, Jefferson County drainage districts, emergency services districts and water control districts. Your address decides which apply.

Properties near the port or the shipping channel may sit inside more special districts than a house in an inland subdivision, so two Beaumont neighbors can pay noticeably different totals on similarly priced homes. Compare your bill with a neighbor's line by line rather than by the bottom number.

If a bill never reaches you, ask the tax office for a copy. Not getting the bill does not stop penalties from starting, so call in January rather than wait. Changing your mailing address with the appraisal district also helps if you have moved or rent the house out.

Reading the city rate

Each fall the city council votes on the city rate, after posting a public notice of that meeting. Call the finance department for the figure that applies to your account.

The city is only one slice of the total. The county, Beaumont ISD and any special district each set a rate of their own every fall. The assessor mails statements in October under state law, and payment is due upon receipt.

  • Find your account on the county tax office website to see what each unit charges on your parcel.
  • Set the City of Beaumont line beside the Beaumont ISD line.
  • Special district lines can differ from one block to the next, so check each.

A homestead exemption cuts the school line, which is why it counts most for a house you live in.

Homestead and over-65 exemptions

An owner who lives in the house on January 1 gets $140,000 off the value used for the school district bill. Those 65 or older, or disabled, get another $60,000 off, and the school tax for them stays at the amount first qualified for. Some surviving spouses aged 55 or more can keep that benefit.

Jefferson CAD warns about companies that mail a designation-of-homestead form and charge a fee to file an application that costs nothing. File directly with the district, which in some cases will also take applications for earlier years.

  • Disabled former service members get exemptions of $5,000 to $12,000 by disability rating, and a 100 percent rating can qualify for a total exemption on the homestead.
  • If the seller never claimed it, a buyer who closes after January 1 can still claim it at once.
  • If an heir is missing from the recorded deed, the filing needs an ownership affidavit, a death certificate and a current utility bill.

Get applications in before May 1, the usual cutoff. Bring a driver's license showing the property address and, if you can, the closing statement from your purchase, and ask the district to confirm in writing once the exemption is posted. Look at your next bill to make sure the school line actually dropped.

When the bill is due, and what late costs

The October bill is payable on arrival, and January 31 is the last day before delinquency. Starting February 1, the account takes a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest. Each month then adds a point of penalty, ending at 12 percent on July 1.

Sheriff's sale announcements appear on the tax office home page. A unit with a contracted collection attorney can add up to 20 percent to accounts still open on July 1. Homeowners who are older, disabled or disabled former service members may split a homestead bill into four installments, and certain collectors extend longer plans.

Unpaid taxes can lead a unit to sue, pile court costs onto the bill and seek foreclosure. Once a homestead is sold at a tax sale, the owner can redeem it for two years after the purchaser's deed is filed, paying a 25 percent premium in year one and 50 percent in year two.

How to protest your appraisal

File a protest with Jefferson CAD by May 15, or within 30 days of getting your value notice when that is later. The district mails homestead notices around April 1 and other notices around May 1.

You will get a hearing date by mail. Arrive with evidence in order and extra copies for the board, and state plainly what value you think is right and your reasons.

Before doing anything else, open your notice; since it shows the market value, the exemptions on file and your deadline. Reasonable grounds are a value that presumes repairs nobody did, storm or flood damage, or a close-by sale that closed below the district's figure. Photos, repair quotes and comparable sales make the case.

If the review board turns you down, you may go to district court, choose binding arbitration, or send a value over $1,000,000 to the State Office of Administrative Hearings.   • Proof of every exemption on the account, so the buyer's escrow is funded correctly.
  • Any installment agreement paperwork, if the account is on a plan.
  • Letters testamentary or an affidavit of heirship for an inherited house.

Give each step time. Request the payoff early; the amount shifts monthly and must hold through your closing day. If the account is on an installment plan, ask the collector what happens to the plan when the house sells.

Liability for a given year's tax stays with whoever held title on January 1, so the settlement statement should spell out which side pays which share. A cash sale skips the lender's review, though the payoff still has to be settled before the deed passes.

Send it to the Jefferson County Tax Assessor-Collector, 1149 Pearl St., Beaumont, 409-835-8516. One payment covers the city, Beaumont ISD and the other units listed.

Under state law the assessor mails bills around October 1, and each is payable on receipt. Ask the tax office if yours is missing.

Beginning February 1 you owe a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest. The penalty grows by a point monthly until July 1, and attorney fees may add up to 20 percent.

How do I get a homestead exemption?

Apply with the Jefferson Central Appraisal District, which takes homestead applications directly at no cost. The house must be your principal residence, and you cannot claim a second homestead elsewhere.

Does the city rate apply to my whole bill?

No. It is one line. Jefferson County, Beaumont ISD and any special district each add their own rate, and your bill shows all of them together.

The calendar on that page lists mid-April for the mailing of notices and May 15 for the protest deadline. The district accepts protests at protest@victoriacad.org. Only the appraisal district can change ownership or the mailing address on a parcel. The tax office will pass a correction along as a courtesy, but a seller who moved or a buyer who just closed should file the change with the appraisal district so the next statement reaches the right person.

The 2026 city rate

City Council approved the FY2027 budget on September 18, 2026, with a 2026 rate of $0.416273 per $100 of property value. The city describes that figure as the no-new-revenue rate, meaning the rate that raises the same revenue as the prior year from properties taxed in both years.

The city's rate is one piece of the bill. Galveston ISD, the county, Galveston College and any special district such as a waterway or drainage district each adopt their own rate. Expect the statement in October and pay before January ends. A postmark after January 31 means penalties, and anything open on February 1 is delinquent, unless you use one of the plans below.

The day after the deadline, a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest attach. From there the penalty adds a point each month, reaching 12 percent on July 1, while interest keeps building monthly with no cap. Selling does not erase a tax debt. Each January 1 a lien secures that year's tax on the parcel, and whoever owned it that day stays liable after any later transfer.

Pull a current statement from the county tax office before you list. Find out too whether your mortgage servicer already paid the bill from escrow. A mortgage code only appears after a lender requests the statement, so sign up for e-statements in the first year after a payoff or refinance so the bill is not missed.

  • If you never had the homestead exemption, the buyer can still claim it for the rest of the year after a closing past January 1.

Yes. Paying half by November 30 leaves the second half open until June 30, with no penalty or interest. Senior, disabled and disabled-veteran homesteads can choose four installments instead, due at the end of January, March, May and July.

Send your application to the appraisal district ahead of May 1 in the tax year it should apply. The district acts within 90 days of receiving the application and will tell you if you do not qualify.

It depends on the street address, because Katy spreads across Fort Bend, Harris and Waller counties. The city's own tax is folded into your county bill. City Hall has not accepted tax payments since September 1, 2015, so every payment goes to a county office:

  • Fort Bend County: 22333 Grand Corner Drive, Katy, phone 281-341-3710
  • Harris County: 16715 Clay Road, Houston, phone 713-368-2000
  • Waller County: 900 13th Street, Hempstead, phone 979-921-0060

Values come from three separate appraisal districts: Fort Bend (281-344-8623), Harris (713-957-7800) and Waller (979-921-0060). If you are unsure of your county, run the address through any district's property search, or look at the collecting office named on a bill you already have.

Katy at a glance

Katy's population is 28,373, a gain of 29.7 percent since 2020. Owners live in about 80.7 percent of homes, and the middle value of an owned home is $401,700. Growth like that is a good reason to read every year's value notice rather than assume the old number still applies.

The 2026 city rate proposal

The city's 2026 notice proposed $0.420000 per $100 of valuation, down from $0.425000 for 2025. It put the no-new-revenue rate at $0.407051 and the voter-approval rate at $0.443092. The proposal sits between the two, so no election was needed. For the final 2026 figure, look at the rate tab on the city's tax information page.

The same notice showed the average homestead taxable value rising from $383,500 in 2025 to $391,368 in 2026. The city's total levy on all properties moved from $25,161,670 to $25,729,208.

The city is only one slice of the bill. The county, school district and any special districts print their rates on the same statement. The notice gives the formula: tax rate times taxable value, divided by 100, with exemptions already taken out of the taxable value. If your value climbs while the rate falls, your city bill can still go up. The city sets the rate, but the three appraisal districts set the values.

What a late Katy tax bill costs

The penalty-free window closes January 31. Starting February 1, the bill picks up a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest, and both climb month by month through July. Not receiving a bill changes nothing: the tax, the due date and the lien stay where they were.

Each January 1 the house becomes security for that year's tax. A Katy sale therefore cannot close cleanly until the year's bill is paid or credited. Request a payoff statement from whichever county bills your address and give it to the title company as soon as you have it.

Owners who are behind have two options. One is a written request to waive penalties, filed inside 181 days of the delinquency date. The other is a payment plan, if the collector offers one.

Lowering your Katy bill

The biggest savings come from two places: the appraisal district and the exemptions you file. Because Katy runs through three counties, you deal with Fort Bend, Harris or Waller depending on where the house sits. Your main choices:

  • School district homestead exemption: $140,000 off value, and another $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners.
  • A city or county exemption, where that unit offers one. State law lets a unit exempt as much as 20 percent of value, with a $5,000 minimum, and the city's terms sit under the Exemption Eligibility tab of Katy's tax page.
  • The 10 percent annual ceiling on homestead value growth, which starts the year after the exemption first applies.
  • A protest filed with the appraisal review board, typically by mid-May.

If the seller never claimed a homestead exemption, a buyer closing after the new year may apply for it immediately.

Selling a Katy house with tax owed

The path is plain. Order the payoff statement from the right county. Look at the city's rate on its tax page. Tell the title company which county holds the parcel, since that decides the collector, the appraisal district and the protest board. A wrong guess costs time.

On closing day the title company takes the amount owed out of your proceeds and divides the current year with the buyer. Selling for cash as-is changes none of this, since the lien must be cleared regardless. If you also plan a protest, tell the title company so the figure used at the table matches the tax bill.

How to pay a Katy property tax bill

Send payment to the collector for your house's county. Fort Bend County takes card or electronic check online. The card fee is 2.29 percent of the total with a $2.75 minimum, electronic checks cost nothing, and business and international cards carry a 3.95 percent fee. Post-dated checks are deposited on receipt, so do not date a check for later.

Questions for the Fort Bend office go to FBCTaxInfo@fortbendcountytx.gov or 281-341-3710. Harris and Waller owners use their own county's collector, listed above. When your lender pays through escrow, check the account online and make sure the payment posted ahead of the January 31 cutoff.

The city's notice also points owners to Texas.gov/PropertyTaxes, a state database of proposed rates and hearings for every unit that taxes your address. If a seller and buyer disagree about who pays what for the year, the title company's settlement statement is where the split gets written down, so check its tax lines before you sign.

Frequently asked questions

Who collects the City of Katy property tax?

Your county's tax office does, because the city charge rides on the county bill. Fort Bend, Harris and Waller each have a payment location listed on the city's tax page.

What rate did Katy propose for 2026?

The city's notice proposed $0.420000 per $100 of valuation, compared with $0.425000 for 2025. Check the city's tax page for the final rate, then add the county, school and special district rates.

When does Katy tax go delinquent?

After January 31. February 1 brings a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent monthly interest, and bills arrive around October 1.

Does Katy offer its own homestead exemption?

The city's tax page has an Exemption Eligibility tab with its terms. The state school exemption is $140,000 on top of that, with $60,000 more for seniors and disabled owners.

Can I protest my Katy appraisal?

Yes, through the appraisal review board of the county that holds your house. The usual deadline falls in mid-May, or 30 days after a late notice.
